THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE N.S.SANJAY GOWDA  ORAL JUDGMENT (PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE N.S.SANJAY GOWDA)
1.
The claimant as well as the insurer are in appeal.
2. The Tribunal has recorded a finding that the deceased Anjayya was hit by the Tata sumo vehicle owned by the first respondent and which was insured by the second respondent.
It has thereafter awarded a sum of Rs.11,69,000/- as compensation.

3. The insurer is an appeal contending that the vehicle that it had insured was not at all involved in the accident, and this becomes clear from the fact that the police records indicated that the cause of the accident was, as a result of a collision by an unknown vehicle with the NC: 2024:KHC-K:6909 deceased.

It is contended that the charge sheet had been filed six months thereafter, implicating the vehicle that the insurer had insured and there was no material at all to indicate as to how this vehicle was found to be the cause of the accident.
It is therefore contended that this was a clear case of implication of a vehicle and therefore, the Tribunal was in error in allowing the claim application.

4. The claimant is also in appeal seeking for enhancement, contending that the amounts determined as notional income was on the lower side and the amounts towards loss of consortium has not been awarded properly.
5.
The owner of the vehicle who had been arrayed as the first respondent before the Tribunal, chose to remain unrepresented and was consequently placed ex-parte.
Thus, the assertion of the claimants that the vehicle owned by the first respondent was involved was not denied by the owner of the vehicle.

The entire case of the insurer is dependent on inferences that are to be drawn NC:
2024:KHC-K:6909 from the police records.
Unless there is clear and positive evidence that the vehicle in question was not involved, this assertion of the insurer cannot be accepted.
6. An argument was also advanced that the IMV report did not indicate any damage to the vehicle.
In a case where a pedestrian was hit by a Tata Sumo, to expect significant damages, which would be visible on the offending vehicle would be unrealistic.

In the light of the fact that the claimants asserted that this particular vehicle was involved and this was based on an investigation conducted Smt Bujjamma W/O Late Anjayya And Ors vs Sant Jagir Singh And Anr on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67072924/
4 by the police, the Tribunal was justified in coming to the conclusion that the vehicle insured by the insurer was indeed involved in the accident.

sentences.text:
7. It may also be relevant to state here that, the insurer did not take the trouble of summoning the investigating Officers and the other personnel involved in the investigation, to elicit from them that the vehicle was implicated.
NC: 2024:KHC-K:6909 8.
In that view of the matter, there is no merit in the appeal of the insurer and the same is accordingly dismissed.
9. As far as the claim for compensation is concerned, the Tribunal has assessed the national income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/-.

Since there was no proof of income, it would be appropriate and prudent to adopt the monthly income determined by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority,
which, for the accident of the year 2015, would be Rs.8,000/- and future prospects of 25% also have to be added to the said sum.
10.
Out of the said sum, 1/4th depending on the number of dependents (Rs.2,500/-) would have to be deducted towards personal expenses of the deceased.
The net income will be Rs.7,500/-.
11. As the deceased was aged 47 years, a multiplier of '13' would have to be applied.

Consequently,
the claimants NC: 2024:KHC-K:6909 would be entitled to a sum of Rs.11,70,000/- (Rs.7,500 x 12 x 13) towards 'loss of dependency'.
12.

The claimants being the father, wife and children of the deceased, each of them would be entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/- towards "loss of consortium" i.e., in all Rs.1,76,000/- and they would also be entitled to a sum of Rs.33,000/- under the "conventional heads".

13. Thus, the claimants, in modification of the impugned award, would be entitled to the following sums :
 Sl. Amount  Nature of Heads  No. (In Rs.)
 1. Loss of Dependency 11,70,000  2. Loss of Consortium 1,76,000  3. Conventional Heads 33,000  Total 13,79,000 14.

Thus, the claimants would be entitled for Smt Bujjamma W/O Late Anjayya And Ors vs Sant Jagir Singh And Anr on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67072924/
5 compensation of Rs.13,79,000/- as against Rs.11,69,000/- awarded by the Tribunal, along with NC: 2024:KHC-K:6909 interest at the rate of six per cent per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
15.

The appeal is accordingly allowed in part.
